**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 12.2(a)(i) already delivers our preferred position on this rule:

- **Customer convenience right exists.** Sanofi may terminate for convenience on written notice, either in its entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis — the partial-termination flexibility the playbook asks for.
- **No Vendor convenience right.** Every RevMed termination trigger is for cause: material breach (12.2(b)), insolvency (12.2(c)), Sanofi's Competing Product (12.2(d)), and Sanofi's cessation of development (12.2(e)). There is no mid-term walk-away for RevMed, so the walk-away scenario in the rule is not present.
- **No early-termination penalty.** The 12.3(c) consequences are a customary grant-back/transition package for a license collaboration, and RevMed actually owes *us* post-termination royalties on Termination Products under 12.3(c)(ii)C — a term that benefits our party and is not flagged.

Two sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted (`[***]`), so the 30-day preferred figure cannot be verified from this draft — worth confirming on the unredacted execution version that it is no longer than 90 days; and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, a concept with little application to a milestone and profit-share structure rather than a prepaid subscription.
